observations: 220 distinct force traces (555,046 scalar samples) for two physical snap joints with a separate numeric outcome vector for each file. Eight MATs contain no synchronized displacement, electrical continuity, or event timestamp. Numeric unit and sample rate are not stated in the archive README, so results are in recorded force units and samples. Numeric label-to-success polarity is not assumed.
ambiguities: README says 50 Training, 60 Testing; actual files have 60 Training and 50 Testing for each joint. Depositor says human (50) and robot (60), while archive README describes human for training and robot for testing. Preserve archive split name and mark physical actor assignment uncertain. Cantilever training has 29 labels 1 and 31 labels 0. Field names skip some integers; match labels positionally to the stored struct order, not by blindly indexing its field suffix. The order pairing has no separate per-trial label key.
method: For each geometry separately, fit four one-feature thresholds using Training only. Select best training balanced accuracy over both directions, midpoints and constant predictors. Evaluate once on the released Testing portion; ties favor above, then lowest threshold. Both signal amplitude and trial length may encode stopping or processing policy; these tests do not timestamp the snap.
findings: The maximum fall from a preceding peak achieves balanced accuracy 0.94 on 50 annular test cases and 0.60 on 50 cantilever test cases using the geometry-specific training threshold. Length alone gives 0.52 and 0.76. These are secondary descriptive baselines using positional labels, not the authors’ classifier.
